inspiration: Creature rows are one flat record each: name, glyph, colour, HP, defence, accuracy, damage range, regen, move speed, attack speed, blood type, light, large flag, drop chance and drop type (monsterCatalog, src/brogue/Globals.c line 1025 onward). Use this as the row-21 field list for our catalogue: one flat row per creature, every number a field, nothing hard-coded in the engine.

Hit chance is accuracy times a defence curve, clamped 0-100, computed in fixed point (src/brogue/Combat.c lines 105-131; defenseFraction in src/brogue/PowerTables.c line 184). Forced hits come first: stuck, captive, seized-and-seizing defenders always get hit (Combat.c lines 110-117). Keep the forced-hit order before the roll for our duel step (row 1).

Replay is an input log, not a frame log: each keystroke and mouse event is written as a compact event, the header stores version, mode, seed, turn count and deepest level in 36 bytes (Recordings.c lines 30, 133-146, 193). Playback reads events back with recallEvent (line 340). Idea for row 19: record the seed and the fight inputs, rebuild the fight on replay.

Glyph-first readability: each creature is one glyph index plus one colour (the ch and color columns). Threat reads from silhouette and colour before any text. Idea for our 375-wide readability: one bold silhouette per creature class, a colour per threat tier, no label needed to tell two enemies apart.

Tiles carry their own light and flags as data: each tile row has a glow light value and a flags and mechFlags pair (tileCatalog, Globals.c lines 315-320). Idea for zone dressing: lights and walkable/blocking flags are per-tile data, so the same tile can glow or block without code changes.

Item kinds are separate variant tables (potion, scroll, wand, charm) selected per build (GlobalsBrogue.c lines 665-713). Idea for loot: keep one table per item family with a shared row shape, and let the variant pick which table is live.

briefs.label: Glyph Skirmisher (own label)
briefs.why: A single bold silhouette in one colour reads at a glance even at 375 wide. The creature row (name, colour, HP, damage range) carries the whole threat story.
briefs.keep: one readable silhouette per creature class; one colour per threat tier; a flat stat row per creature
briefs.change: ours is a sprite with a head-and-shoulders silhouette and a limb shape, not a glyph; our palette is ours; stat names and numbers are ours
briefs.ref: src/brogue/Globals.c line 1025 (monsterCatalog) and the rat/kobold/jackal rows directly under it

briefs.label: Lit Hazard Tile (own label)
briefs.why: A tile that carries its own light and its own walkable or blocking flags lets a zone look dangerous without a single line of code.
briefs.keep: per-tile glow value; per-tile flags for block and hazard; one table of tile rows
briefs.change: our tiles are zone data with our own names; the glow colour is ours; the hazard is a fire or fog tile we author, not the donor's tile set
briefs.ref: src/brogue/Globals.c lines 315-320 (tileCatalog header row with light and flags columns)
